children: Shares of telecommunications and cable services provider Optimum Communications

jumped 5.9% in the afternoon session after the company signed an expanded, multi-year distribution agreement with A+E Global Media. According to Streetinsider, Optimum Communications and A+E Global Media announced a renewed and expanded deal that keeps Optimum TV subscribers across the company’s 21-state footprint able to access A+E’s full linear channel lineup, including A&E, The History Channel, Lifetime, Lifetime Movie Network, FYI, VICE, Military History Channel, Crime + Investigation, Lifetime Real Women, and The History Channel en Español. Multi-year carriage deals help cable operators protect their programming slate and reduce the risk of channel blackouts that can push subscribers to cancel or switch providers.
What Is The Market Telling Us

Optimum Communications’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 68 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 27 days ago when the stock gained 4.9% on the news that the company announced the completion of a $6 million investment to strengthen its network infrastructure in Lubbock, Texas. According to the company’s press release, the project includes the construction of an approximately 100-mile fiber ring designed to power the local network backbone. The network upgrade delivers enhanced performance across the city, providing faster and more reliable connectivity for residential neighborhoods, small businesses, fire stations, and essential public facilities. The infrastructure enhancements support the company's efforts to modernize broadband capabilities and improve network reliability across the region.

Optimum Communications is down 37.5% since the beginning of the year, and at $1.08 per share, it is trading 60% below its 52-week high of $2.69 from October 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Optimum Communications’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $52.24.
